I am playing Monopoly as an AI player.

I have $179 and two mortgaged yellows. The opponent has $1082 and owns most of the board, including orange hotels. I cannot build or trade until I unmortgage.

I just passed GO and paid income tax, leaving me with $179. I am deciding whether to unmortgage a yellow property or end my turn. I want to keep my yellows intact and build a cash cushion for dangerous rent.

I mapped the board positions. Rolling from Income Tax lands on Oriental, Vermont, Connecticut, and Jail.

Rolling 11 lands on Pennsylvania Railroad for $200, which I cannot afford. Rolling 12 lands on St James Place with a hotel for $950, which is impossible to pay. Unmortgaging Ventnor would raise my cash by only $130, so it is not enough to survive these dangerous spaces.

Unmortgaging Ventnor would raise cash to $309, enough to cover the $200 Pennsylvania Railroad rent but still not enough for the $950 orange hotel rent. I cannot survive a roll of 12 from Income Tax. I am now considering trading properties to raise cash, though surviving orange hotels may be impossible with my current holdings.

I checked the other players' holdings. p1 does not own yellows, so they likely want them. p2 owns browns with hotels and all four railroads. I am weighing trade offers to raise cash.

Unmortgaging one yellow leaves the set incomplete, so building is impossible. All three yellows would cost $308 to unmortgage, which exceeds my $179. I am extremely weak and cannot afford the dangerous orange hotels or four railroads.

I am now calculating the probability of dying on St James Place. If I cannot pay the $950 rent, p1 would take my yellows and likely win the game.

Mortgaging Ventnor would reduce the fatal roll 12 probability to one in thirty-six. Even then, the board remains lethal because p1 owns three orange hotels and p2 owns brown hotels plus four railroads. I am now mapping the full circuit danger to decide whether to unmortgage or end my turn.

I am weighing whether to mortgage Ventnor to survive the next roll. I also suspect p1 may try to buy a yellow property to break my monopoly.

I realized that selling my yellows to p2 would give them a yellow monopoly and the ability to build hotels. That could be my only way to raise enough cash to survive, but it would also eliminate my own win condition. With only $179 and no houses, I cannot win unless both other players go bankrupt, which seems unlikely.

I am calculating the exact cost to unmortgage all three yellows: $308 total, $129 short of my current cash. Mortgage Ventnor does not help because it is one of the three properties. I am now estimating rent returns from building houses and hotels on yellows, with hotels yielding $1150–$1275 per space.

Building houses on all three yellows would cost $1350, which I cannot afford. Even one house per property would only raise rent to about $90–$100, too little to threaten the other players. I am now weighing two concrete choices: end my turn with $179 and hope to avoid rolling 11 or 12, or mortgage Ventnor for $309 and survive that roll but lose Ventnor’s rent.

I am now considering a trade with p2. If I sell all three yellows to them, they would gain a yellow monopoly and I would receive cash. However, without any properties left, I would still be unable to survive the orange hotels.

I realized that selling my yellows would only delay bankruptcy, not win the game. The cash needed to unmortgage and build all three yellows exceeds $750, which p2 will not give me for free. I also considered trading with p1, but they already own orange hotels and would likely not pay enough to make the set dangerous.

I am now checking every landing spot from Income Tax with $309 cash. Rolling 2 lands on Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut, all owned by p1 without houses. The rent is only $12 to $24, so I can afford it. I also noted that rolling 3 hits a Chance card.

Rolls 6 through 10 from Income Tax are all safe. St Charles, States, and Virginia each cost $20. Virginia costs $24. The electric company is mortgaged and costs nothing. I am now reviewing the two Chance cards.

I am now evaluating the two Chance cards. One sends me to Boardwalk, which costs $50 without a monopoly. Another sends me to Illinois or St Charles for $20 each. The nearest railroad from this Chance is Pennsylvania RR.

I checked the "go back 3 spaces" Chance card. From this position it lands on Oriental, not Baltic. Baltic has a hotel for $450, but that is irrelevant here.

The other Chance cards are harmless. Paying $50 to each opponent costs $100, which I can afford at either cash level. Advancing to GO yields $200. Boardwalk and Illinois cost only $50 and $20 respectively. No Chance card sends me to a hotel.

I am now tallying the exact fatal landing spots from Income Tax. Rolling 11 or 3 plus a nearest-railroad Chance both cost $200, which is fatal at $179 but survivable at $309. Rolling 12 is fatal either way. I am also checking how many of the sixteen standard Chance cards advance to the nearest railroad.

Only two of the sixteen Chance cards advance to the nearest railroad, so that risk is minor. The real danger is rolling 11 or 12. Mortgage Ventnor for $309 would survive the 11, but Ventnor’s rent is only $22 because the yellow monopoly is incomplete.

The log shows Ventnor rent was $44, not the standard $22. I will trust that figure. The expected income from keeping it unmortgaged is roughly $22 to $44 per landing, though opponents land there only rarely.

The expected income from keeping Ventnor is negligible. If I die to p2 on the railroad, they would gain my yellows and use them to build hotels and crush p1. If I die to p1 on St James, they would also take my yellows and become more dominant. Mortgaging Ventnor prevents p2 from stealing my yellows on a railroad hit, so I keep them if I survive. The only remaining fatal roll is St James, which p1 owns. This makes mortgaging Ventnor the clear correct choice.

I am now calculating the exact cash shortfall to survive St James Place. With $179 I need $771 more, and with $309 I still need $641. No opponent will trade me that much cash for nothing, so raising funds through trades is impossible.

Selling all yellows to p2 would give me cash but leave me propertyless, so I would still die to the orange hotels. p1 would not overpay for a single yellow, and breaking the set by selling Ventnor would yield too little cash. The only viable trade is asking p2 for enough money to survive, in exchange for my promise not to go bankrupt to p1.

I am now calculating the exact survival probability. The orange hotels on St James, Tennessee, and New York Avenue each charge $950, while Boardwalk costs only $50 because Park Place is mortgaged. Accumulating enough cash to unmortgage and build all three yellows seems extremely unlikely.

I am now tallying the exact dangerous landing spots. Nine of the forty spaces charge over $200 in rent, including the four railroads and the orange hotels. The greens are safe because they are mortgaged. This leaves only about nine deadly spaces total, though three of them are my own yellows.

A full circuit from $309 would net only about $200 after taxes and rent, so surviving by accumulating cash is impossible. The only remaining paths are a trade that creates a winning position or playing for chaos and hoping the other players bankrupt each other. p1 has orange hotels, while p2 has $948 and will hit those same oranges; p1 also has $1082 and will land on brown hotels and railroads.

p2 is on North Carolina with $948. An orange hotel costs $950, so p2 cannot pay it and is one bad roll away from bankruptcy to p1. From this position, rolling 2 lands on a Community Chest, 3 on Pennsylvania Avenue (mortgaged), 4 on Short Line, and 5 on a Chance card.

p2 is not immediately on the orange hotels. From North Carolina they must circle the board, so p1 has more time to survive. p1 is safer with $1082 than p2 with $948. I will mortgage Ventnor to survive the railroad hit and keep my yellows from p2. I am now considering whether p2 might offer a trade that helps me more.

I rejected the idea of giving p2 yellows, since that would let them build hotels and kill p1 while I still die. I also dismissed trading mortgaged yellows for unmortgaged properties, because p1 would not offer useful income-generating assets. Proposing to p2 for cash without immediate compensation is certain to be rejected. The only remaining option is to sell the yellows at a price that bankrupts or weakens p2 against p1.

I rejected the idea of selling yellows to p2 for cash. That would leave me propertyless and bankruptable, and p2 would likely bankrupt to p1 instead. The strategy is too convoluted.

Mortgaging Ventnor is the clear best move to survive the $200 railroad hit. I can only take one action per decision, but the engine will ask again if more remain. I am weighing whether to trade first while Ventnor is still unmortgaged, or mortgage it for safety and trade later. No opponent currently holds a red monopoly.

p1 could unmortgage Pacific and Pennsylvania to build green houses, but that is a future move. I will mortgage Ventnor now. I am also drafting a public message that does not reveal my weakness.

Unmortgaging Atlantic Avenue would leave only $36 and leave the yellow set incomplete, so that is a dead end. I briefly considered trading with p2 for cash or with p1 for orange hotels, but those offers are unappealing to both sides.
